claims.text: These three artifacts are all for the same trip: the trip_record (TRP-00510, booked 2026-08-29T09:05:00, accepted 09:05:40), the driver's gps_trace (first fix 09:11:40, last fix 09:30:40) and the fare_breakdown (TRP-00510, charged 09:31:00) carry matching identifiers and a consistent pickup-to-charge sequence. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) to show the artifacts describe one trip is therefore discharged on the face of the record.

The deviation clears both establishment tests in POL-RD-01. The governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which records 8.8 km against a booked optimal of 6.2 km from the routing engine — an excess of 2.6 km, or 41.94% of optimal. Both the 0.8 km absolute test and the 20% relative test are passed, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The excess must be measured on the trace figure, not on trip_record.actual_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 marks as a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test.

Nothing about this trace needs corroboration, because it is not impaired. It carries 115 fixes across the full 19-minute trip at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, an expected interval of 10 seconds, an empty gaps list and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) conditions — a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 seconds — is met, so the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The driver's own counterparty statement removes any doubt about the cause of the excess: he says he 'missed the exit' and 'looped back right away'. That is an admission, on the record, that the vehicle left the optimal corridor — and it sits alongside a trace showing the car never exceeding a minimum separation of 0.92 m from the booked line at booking, then running 8.8 km against a 6.2 km optimal. Where the trace is unimpaired the admission is not strictly needed, but it forecloses any suggestion that the excess is a measurement artefact.

No traffic advisory covers the optimal corridor for this trip window. Artifact EV-ADVIS-00510-01 is MISSING — it has no payload, its admissibility status is MISSING and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, with the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT recorded. I disclose that impairment expressly. Because there is no advisory record that names a road the optimal route traverses, carries an overlapping validity window and is matched by a leave-and-rejoin pattern, POL-RD-03 exoneration cannot be run at all on this record, and the missing advisory supplies no amended optimal route and no reduction of the excess.

The in-app chat export for this trip is empty: message_count is 0, the messages array is empty and no first or last message timestamp exists. There is accordingly no rider instruction, no named road and no waypoint_hint capable of satisfying POL-RD-04(a) to (c), and the rider-requested detour route of exoneration is unavailable to the driver. The pol_rd_11_remedy note itself records that nothing in this trip reads the chat log.

No endpoint was relocated. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 therefore has nothing to re-apply and cannot reduce the excess, and equally there is no missing re-quote to trigger POL-RD-10(5).

This was not a pooled trip. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the 6.2 km routing-engine figure is the correct baseline for the POL-RD-01 comparison. No part of the 2.6 km excess can be excused as co-rider collection or set-down.

The fare was fixed at booking: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted_fare_sgd of 15.80. POL-RD-02 therefore does not run and no distance-or-time recomputation is made; the rider's remedy is the one POL-RD-11 provides, namely the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09.

No pass-through line reduces that entitlement. There are no ERP gantries on the trip (erp_gantries is empty and the erp_lines and off-optimal-route totals are all 0.00), tolls_erp is 0.00, waiting_time_fee is 0.00, and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that originates at Blk 79 Toa Payoh Central and ends at Kallang MRT rather than originating at any airport. The properly_chargeable total is therefore 0.00 and the rider's entitlement is not eroded by any of it.

On those figures the rider was overcharged by exactly SGD 10.00: charged_total 25.80, less quoted_fare_sgd 15.80, less properly chargeable pass-throughs of 0.00, equals 10.00, which is what the platform's own derived pol_rd_11_remedy field publishes for this case. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the rider is presently carrying that overcharge and the claim that the app quietly charged more than the fixed price is made out on the ledger. The rider asks for that 10.00 back under POL-RD-11(a).

No rider-side corroboration gate applies. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition that requires extra corroboration (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met, and there is nothing on this profile that can be read against the claim. I note for completeness that the remaining profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01 and I cite none of them as a ground of decision.

This is a case the tribunal can decide, not hold. The trace is clean under POL-RD-07, every contested artifact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, no party has asserted a closure against the missing advisory artifact (and POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire), the identifiers all match, and timestamps run forward. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers is present, so ESCALATE would be wrong here: the disputed amount should be refunded to the rider rather than held.

Finally, everything the ruling rests on is clean evidence at full weight: the trip_record, gps_trace, fare_breakdown and chat_log are all admissibility status COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes. The only artifact below 1.0 in this bundle is the MISSING traffic advisory at weight 0.0, which carries no fact and is cited here only for its absence. No disclosure discount under POL-GEN-02 is owed on any fact that decides this case.

claims.text: The excess on this trip is real but modest. The governing trace measures 8.8 km against a 6.2 km platform optimal, an excess of 2.6 km or 41.94%, which clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km) but falls short of the clause's MATERIAL gate, which requires an excess greater than 50% of optimal or greater than 8.0 km absolute. I accept the deviation is established on the driver's own trace; it is not material, and the enhanced consequences POL-RD-01 reserves for a material deviation simply do not arise on this record.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be found against this driver on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250, so neither limb of the pattern test fires: 0 is below the threshold of 3, and 0/250 is 0.00, below the 0.05 ratio, with the 40-trip minimum on the denominator satisfied. It follows that neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available, and no seriousness can be inferred from this driver's history. driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a LIFETIME counter and is context only under POL-GEN-01; it is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names.

This trip was booked on an UPFRONT_QUOTE with fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 15.80, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. On an upfront-quoted trip the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and the detour costs the rider nothing on those lines. The rider's pleaded theory — that the missed exit means the whole charge should be reversed — therefore fails as a matter of policy, not merely on the numbers: the rider claims SGD 25.80 on a route-deviation ground that POL-RD-11 closes.

On the ledger the rider's recovery is capped at the arithmetic line in POL-RD-11(a), and nothing more: charged_total of SGD 25.80 less the quoted fare of SGD 15.80, with properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines under POL-RD-09 of SGD 0.00, leaves SGD 10.00 as the ceiling. The remaining SGD 15.80 the rider asks for is not a remedy the policy provides on an upfront-quoted fare, and the contested amount of SGD 25.80 overstates the maximum exposure by that margin.

There is no billing-integrity defect on this fare to add anything on top of that ceiling. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge line, and the trip neither originates at Changi nor Seletar, so POL-RD-09(4) yields nothing and no phantom-gantry or surcharge referral arises; the waiting-time fee is SGD 0.00 as well, so there is no properly chargeable statutory or pass-through line to be added back against the rider. Nothing on this ledger is chargeable back to the driver beyond the capped POL-RD-11(a) line.

The trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes, so this case is decidable on the record and no data-failure route to escalation is open. EV-GPS-00510 carries 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence with coverage of 100%, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07's limbs (a) to (c) fires; no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) cannot be triggered. The trip identifiers also match across EV-TRIP-00510, EV-GPS-00510 and EV-FARE-00510, so POL-RD-10(2) does not fire, and the refund in issue is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6). The case should be ruled on its merits and capped at the figure above rather than held for a human reviewer.

I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00510-01 is a MISSING artifact: it has no payload, carries weight_multiplier 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. That absence does not escalate this dispute. POL-RD-03 is not invoked by anyone — the driver's account is that he missed an exit, not that any road, segment or junction was closed — so there is no asserted external traffic cause for POL-RD-08 or POL-RD-13 to weigh and no exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5). The driver rests on no advisory and asks for no exoneration under POL-RD-03; the case should therefore be decided on the merits, with the rider limited to the POL-RD-11(a) figure.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling decides the SGD 25.80 contested on trip TRP-00510, and it is addressed to both of you.

WHAT HAPPENED. The booking was an upfront-quoted fare: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 15.80 (EV-FARE-00510). The driver missed an exit and looped back — his own statement concedes the missed exit, and that account is accepted. The platform's trace (EV-GPS-00510) measures 8.8 km against the 6.2 km routing-engine optimal, an excess of 2.6 km / 41.94%. That clears both establishment tests in POL-RD-01 (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It falls short of the MATERIAL gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so the enhanced consequences POL-RD-01 reserves for material deviations do not arise. Both advocates' claims on this point are accepted, in the same terms.

WHY THE DEVIATION DOES NOT SET THE MONEY. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, and the detour therefore costs the rider nothing on those lines. That is the driver's point and it is correct; it is also the rider's own concession, and it is why the rider's pleaded request for the whole charge to be reversed fails as a matter of policy, not merely on the numbers.

THE FIGURES. POL-RD-11(a) refunds the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quoted fare plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. charged_total = SGD 25.80; quoted_fare_sgd = SGD 15.80; properly chargeable = SGD 0.00 (no ERP gantries on the trip, erp_lines and off-optimal totals all 0.00, no airport surcharge — this trip neither originates at Changi nor Seletar — and waiting_time_fee SGD 0.00). 25.80 − 15.80 − 0.00 = SGD 10.00, which is exactly what the platform's own derived pol_rd_11_remedy publishes. The rider is refunded SGD 10.00. The further SGD 15.80 the rider asks for is not a remedy the policy provides on an upfront-quoted fare, and the contested figure of SGD 25.80 overstates the maximum exposure by that margin.

NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. POL-RD-04's compensation limb does not fire: the fare breakdown's charged distance (8.8 km) is not less than the trace distance (8.8 km), so there is no unbilled shortfall. The exoneration limbs of POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 are all unavailable — no advisory invokes POL-RD-03, the chat log is empty so no rider-requested detour exists, no pin was amended, and this was a RYDE_X solo trip rather than a pool — and, because POL-RD-11 governs, their exoneration would not change the money in any event.

NO ESCALATION.
